title: THE BIBLE : THE BOOK OUR OF FATHERS | Traumatizing Knees Of Pressure !! (Part 3)

sense.text:
I also will do this unto you: Because we, the Israelites, we broke the laws of the Most High. We refuse to keep his commandments, and these commandments that God gave us was based on conditions, meaning that we had to keep the laws in order to inherit the blessings, and if we broke the laws we would receive the curses. So this is what happened to the 12 tribes of Israel.

I will even appoint over you terror: So this is the reason why this series is labeled the Traumatizing Knees of Pressure, because this pressure brings the terror upon us.

I will even appoint over you terror: I will even appoint unto you Israelites, you disobedient Israelites, I will appoint unto you terror. And this is exactly what we've experienced, and we continue to experience that thing, because we are still in the action of not repenting. We're still going away from the Most High. The Most High is going to continue to turn the heat up on us until we realize our offense and acknowledge it and return unto him.

Terror: So the point that I want to draw out of there is the terror. The Most High said he's going to put terror on us. Now last week we talked about Derek Chauvin when he was in the courtroom, and you had the sister Darnella, who was 17 at the time, and I wanted to draw points to what you actually saw on YouTube and what she actually saw in the actual court. Because YouTube has scaled the picture down, for you not to see where Derek Chauvin's knee was literally pressed upon George Floyd's neck. He was squeezed into the pavement. They didn't show that on the YouTube, but the sister saw that in the courtroom, because that was actually her phone. So when the attorney said, can you put up exhibit, I forget the number of it, but when he put the exhibit up there and it had Derek Chauvin's face looking directly at the sister, she saw a maniac. She saw a terrorist. She saw a murdering maniac. That's what she saw. She saw the whole picture. She didn't just see his torso. She saw his head, his knees. She saw George Floyd's face smashed into the ground. She saw all of that, and that's the reason why she was terribly traumatized.

Terror: This is what she saw, but they didn't show this on the YouTube video. That's what I want y'all to understand. Like I did last week, I said zoom in. When I said zoom in, you can see, look how bad that thing looks. This is what she saw, and she was absolutely terrified. Look how calm he is. This is the terror that has been put over our people.

Terror: This terror that Chauvin did in front of witnesses, in front of the kids, in front of Darnella, everybody's minds is super messed up now because of this terrorist act that was done. So the judge was, quote unquote, forced to look at other aggravating factors. Normally this would have not even been mentioned, but there's so much that could happen on the backside of things. They say, you know what, we better dig a little deeper and completely throw the book at this guy. He's going to be the fall guy for the whole deal, because that doesn't change the racist policies of this country. Don't be fooled by that. Although we're looking at this particular situation here, the point is to burn Chauvin to win the love of Negroes.

Terror: Y'all see what's happening here? They said the aggravating factors, in addition to George Floyd being murdered, it said that he abused his position of trust. That's what they call public trust. He abused that. He also treated Floyd with particular cruelty, meaning that's that indifference, when you have no empathy, no sympathy, nothing. You're thinking that he's just totally an alien to you, where you don't have to share any human characteristics with them. That's what that part means.

Terror: When it says particular cruelty, this is what it means, and this is what Darnella was witnessing. He wouldn't do his son like that. He wouldn't do his own people that way. That's what the particular cruelty is. And again, don't get twisted off of thinking that all of a sudden America falling in love with you so-called Blacks and Hispanics. That's not what's happening here. So don't fall asleep on that, because this is obvious. You look at this here: they don't do white folks like this here. They don't do their own like this here. White folks walk through open areas with AK-47s, anything, and it's no prob. They talk them down. Dylann Roof: that preacher in North Carolina, I forget his name, that preacher that we had on a few weeks ago, he said that Dylann Roof killed and murdered folk, and he got arrested. He didn't die. He didn't get murdered. He didn't get shot, tased, nothing, and went to the Burger King because he was hungry. George Floyd asked for water. He asked for air. That's the particular cruelty and the indifference.

Terror: The reason why I'm bringing these points up is because Derek Chauvin didn't learn this in a vacuum. Do you kind of see how the media is zeroing in solely on the police? They're making you think that the police is the culprit and everybody else is about justice. Derek Chauvin did not learn his inhumane actions toward George Floyd on his own, or he didn't just, quote unquote, learn it from the police department. That was bred in him in this society, and that's what we're gonna talk about in the few parts of these videos.

Terror: You say he already had it in him. So if he already had it in him, because that's obvious, and we're gonna prove that he already had it in him, if he already had it in him, why is this social engineering trying to focus us to only look at one segment of the whole tree? That's the point. Because you got to look at the totality of the whole thing. Just imagine if he was a doctor. That ain't got nothing to do with police. He would have been jacking Black people up in the hospitals. What if he would have been a teacher? He would have been lying and teaching. He would have dealt with the children scholastically the same way that you see him physically, with this particular cruelty that he did to George Floyd. That's what we would have witnessed. If he was selling ice cream, you'd probably drop the ice cream and then put it on the cone and give it to you. So that hatred and terror is in them, and it is bred, it's inbred in them, and the society gave them the authority to be that way. It encouraged them, and that's what we're gonna show you. I hope you brothers and sisters understand that. Don't fall asleep on what the judge did.

Terror: The children were present at the time. That is the same comparison that we talked about with Willie Lynch, when our sister was tied to a tree and cut open, and they made children watch. That is a level of trauma, that is a level of cruelty that these babies had to witness and carry inside of them. So how in the world you're just going to say that's Derek? Your whole history lends to that kind of treatment. We never really got over that trauma. That trauma was passed through. Like I said last week, we were fed punk milk from that time, from when the fear and terror would cross through the veins of our mothers and through our fathers and brought it all the way down, and we come out terrorized. We scratch when we don't itch. Can you dig it? We're looking all down to white folks. All of that is because that is inbred. We learn that. We just have this subservient feeling that's not natural. That was part of the curriculum of America, and that's the reason why these things are happening. So don't just put this on Chauvin. Chauvin is a part of the old American way.

Terror: The aggravating factors: abuse of trust, or public trust, as a peace officer, police officer. You get the public's trust, and they sway you in on that. That's what that's talking about. He also treated George Floyd with particular cruelty, meaning not human. This is outside of the scope of dealing with human beings. He dealt with George Floyd as if he was some animal, or gorilla in the midst, the same thing like they dealt with Rodney King. That's the reason why I made that comparison to Rodney King. They dealt with him just like that. They were tased, they were trying to break his legs, meanwhile they had a rope around his neck. That's in the video. If you watch the video again, you will actually see one of the white officers was at a far distance, almost out of the frame of the camera, but you can see he just pulled on the rope every time Rodney King tried to get up. When he tried to get up, he pull it to make him fall again. And they're saying, oh, he was trying to attack the police, when he was actually trying to escape death. That's what you saw. So again, that's particular cruelty. How come these aggravating factors were not put in the Rodney King trial? How come that didn't come up?

Terror: Rodney King ended up dying in a swimming pool, and he was a better than average swimmer, because he was learning that for his therapy, therapy for what had happened to him. So he knew how to swim. So all of a sudden he's at the bottom of the pool dead, because those demons, when I say demons, meaning the conscience. The conscience of us tells us, why are we in this condition? Why is it that I had to be called a gorilla in the midst? They call me a lizard and beat me half to death and all of that. And you wrestle with that thing, and some of us think that our skin is the reason for it, just like the sister Serena Williams, this tennis player. She bleach her skin because she wants to get away from the stigma. What stigma? This is this color that God gave us. But you can see how this trauma turns our mind inside out. So Rodney King was struggling with that thing, and I imagine, because I don't have the absolute facts, I imagine that he said, you know what, that's it, I can't take no more.

Terror: When we watch the movie Them, this movie that's been out recently, there's a character, I forget the character's name, the blackface character, and he said, what you gonna do? That's what our conscience does to us every time we suffer a level of discrimination, when we get the disrespect, when our families get disrespected, when our women get disrespected. You walking down the street with your wife and some white man put his hands all over her, and here you supposed to be the man. Then your conscience gonna be like, yo, what you gonna do? And after constantly hearing that voice, you want to tell the voice to shut up. Not really, because you know the voice is right, but you feel like you have no power to change it. So that duality is wrestling inside your head. You're conflicted in your life, and that's where the drugs come in. That's where the dope comes in, because you need something to stop the voices. Many people go into the psychiatric units with these kinds of voices going on in their minds. I've seen many of them, so I know what I'm talking about when it comes to that.

Terror: It's not fiction. This ain't fiction. This is what goes on in Black people's minds every time we get disrespected. That duality, this is what I'm talking about. That's his conscience. His wife was harassed, supervisor jerked him out of a position, all that. So all of these things was going on in his mind, and that's with his conscience beating him. Rodney King went through the same damn thing. That's the point I'm bringing out. This is what's going through his mind. That's what's going on with our Black men, and many of us, because we're struggling trying to find the solution to these problems, and we're going about it all the wrong way.

Terror: There were children present during the crime. That's the trauma, just like Willie Lynch. Committed crime as a group: that's where the other defendants are going to get caught up in this thing, because they were part of it.

Terror: You hear what she's saying? She's saying that in cases like this, normally, according to what they're saying, there's normally five aggravating factors that you can use to change the sentencing up. The judge have come back and said we got four of them, and this woman is saying you only need one. So let's see what happens. Again, don't you Negroes get happy, because like I said on many occasions, they'll burn the hell out of one to put millions of you to sleep. You still got a whole lot of cases that's going on right now that ain't trying to deal with it, or no justice level at all currently.

Terror: This is the white man saying this. Everybody on the side saw exactly what he's reading, but they experienced it and saw it happen in real time. The judge is looking at it after the fact, but imagine seeing what you actually read in there actually was happening. Let that part marinate. The slow death: that's torture. That's terror. Was particularly cruel: meaning that it is beyond the scope of human cruelty. This is particularly cruel, like animals. In that Mr. Floyd was begging for his life: and Chauvin still remained to keep the pressure on him, although EMTs was telling him, the martial artist was telling him, George Floyd's friend was telling him, get off of him, check his pulse, he can't breathe, all those things, while that 10 year old girl saw that. Just think about all that terror that went down.

Terror: It says that he was begging for his life and obviously terrified by the knowledge that he was likely to die. That's the part that I was making when I was talking about the scared stares of our sister being tied on that tree, when I mentioned the Willie Lynch situation, where the woman was tied to a tree and a white maniac cut her stomach open and pulled the baby out. And the records said that the scared stares of the people watching her could not help her, and she could acknowledge that she was going to die simply by looking at the fear in their eyes. That's what's being said here, that he was obviously terrified by the knowledge of knowing that he was likely to die. But during which the defendant, Derek Chauvin, objectively remained indifferent, meaning I don't give a damn, because I'm gonna get a hard on by killing you, and I'm gonna go home and blaze the wife up. This is my aphrodisiac. Black death is America's fetish. There's a fetish to this country. Indifferent to Mr. Floyd's pleas: please, I can't breathe.

Terror: As you can see, people are actually more happy because of that one situation. Like I said, he's going to be the example. They're going to burn his behind with that thing, because like I said last week, the man was crying for his mama. They probably told him, listen, we can't cover this up. The man was crying for his mama, and you did it in front of kids. What the hell was wrong with you? We can't cover you. That's when the union walk out. Trust me, I know how that works. The union walk out, people be like, listen, you're on your own, we can't help you.

Terror: The reason why I'm bringing this out is because I'm going to draw back to the point that you made about Chauvin: had he been a doctor, had he been an ice cream man, whatever, those same racist feelings and actions, the terror would have been in him regardless of what it is. So don't merely just look at a police educating medium. All of the mediums in this society cause these people to think this way. So don't fall asleep, brothers and sisters. Now they're talking about reforming police policies as if that's the answer.

Terror: See, that's why I said don't get too happy, brothers and sisters. Right after the we can breathe, all that exuberance, six more people died after the verdict unjustly. That's the point that's being made there. So again, like I said, they're looking to somewhat throw a soft book at Chauvin, because they ain't really going to get them the way they're supposed to get them. And that's just one. Like that graph that I showed last week, from 2005 to 2015, it was a ten year span where no policemen were accused of murder in terms of these shootings.

Terror: He said after you have a high profile situation, the Department of Justice comes in, move some things around, and then boom, you got another killing. Then some time pass, DOJ come back in again, boom, another killing. So in other words, nothing's changing. That's the point that he's making.

Terror: Even though the brother said some great points, he still focused it on the police. He said, will this change police, as if that's where the whole crux is. Systematic level: the police department is not the whole system. The police department is just one peg out of many pegs that make up the entire system. Like I said before, this is one of those cases where you got to get to the root of it all. You got to get to the cause of it all.

Terror: He said you're not dealing with bad apples, because everyone's focusing on a Derek Chauvin here, these guys in New York, Volpe, the different cops that be doing different things. Those are, quote unquote, the bad apples. But people are thinking that it's a good tree that just happened to have bad apples. Trevor is saying something totally different. They're going to misquote what he just said for political reasons. I'll leave it that way. So the focus should not be on the bad apples. That's what Trevor's saying. You're busy focusing on the bad apples. Trevor is saying, forget about the fruit that the rotten tree bears. You gotta look at the tree itself.

For every tree is known by his own fruit: For every tree is known by the rotten apples. So if you got rotten apples, a few bad apples, you gotta look at the tree that bore the apples, and the tree is what we want to talk about now. Not just the branch. The tree has many branches. One of the branches is the police department, but the branch does not bring the tree. The tree brings the branches. So now you got to look at the tree. You have to look at the soil that the tree was planted in. You got to look at all of that, and that's what's going to determine what kind of fruit is going to be born from the tree.

Neither doth a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit: He just took what Trevor Noah said and boiled it all the way down to a police matter, and said that we are looking to reform all this police stuff. How in the world could you, quote unquote, reform a police department to be the way you would expect it to be, and the rest of the tree is still rotten? That's not going to work. It simply won't work. Just like I made the point about the engine: the different parts of the engine work together for the operation of the entire motor. You can't talk about changing the pistons and turning it into something; the engine ain't gonna work. You got to tear the whole engine down. That's what Trevor was saying without saying it.

Neither doth a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit: You have a store. You have the human resources, you have the security, or the police within the store, you have the salesmen, you have the stock people. You got all the different components that work together. You got the people to bring the groceries in. You got so many segments that operate within this to make the supermarket be the supermarket. If you take one part of it and twist it, it's going to affect the entire supermarket. You can't just isolate and say that it's only this. All of it works in a system in order for the supermarket to work. So you just can't, quote unquote, reform the police department and not deal with the rest of the educating mediums of the society. I was trying to give the analogy of the store. I don't think I made a good analogy with that, but when I'm done with this here, you're gonna understand exactly what I mean when I say that you just cannot take a, quote unquote, police department and say, oh, we're making reforms, we're making changes, as if that's going to alleviate all of this injustice and evil. It's not going to work.

Neither doth a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit: He mentioned so many different segments that he said have something to do with the corruptness that's going on there. Well, where did they learn all of this at? You talking about IT, you're talking about hiring practices, HR. These people don't carry guns or walk the street arresting people. These people are sitting in air-conditioned offices pushing papers around, who to hire, who to promote, and everybody got a problem. So it's not, quote unquote, the police department per se. If you're talking about it just on that level, that goes pervasive throughout the whole society.

Neither doth a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit: These police will be retaliated against. That's garbage that's upstream that's going to come down to mess these, quote unquote, good apples up. So it's not going to work. The whole stuff, Babylon got to be destroyed. That's the only way this thing gonna fix. Other than that, all of this, it don't mean nothing. Now I will say this here, because I know somebody might be saying, well, what do they want? Like I said before, any measure of justice for George Floyd's family, for anybody, that we get, we gladly take it. All praises to the Most High. Any breath of justice, we'll take it. Our people will take it. Protest, do what you got to do, take it. Whatever relief that we can get, all praises. But that is not going to fix our problem. In other words, don't stop there. You got to come to the scriptures. Understand the reason why all of this is happening. Repent, and the Most High will bless us and get us the hell out of here. That's what we have to do.

The wicked are estranged from the womb: Had he been a doctor, had he been a teacher, had he been this and that, his racism and his terrorism would have came out regardless. It would have came out in another form, but it would have still come out. And the reason for that is because the incubator that these people are made in causes them to be the way they are, because it's in them. I'm not saying that they were influenced by some alien force. They themselves are evil. This is what the problem is. This is the first thing we have to understand and not fall asleep on.

The wicked are estranged from the womb: Estranged, meaning off the path of righteousness. Estranged meaning different. Estranged meaning outside of the parameters of righteousness. Where do they become a stranger? Where do they become killers? From the womb. They were born wicked. That's what the Most High say. They're natural born killers. That's what the Most High is telling you right there out of that Bible.

They go astray as soon as they be born: The minute they come out, they're criminals. The minute they come out.

Their poison is like the poison of a serpent: That's what happened to Serena Williams, listening to this Edomite. That philosophy made her change her whole body up.

Their poison is like the poison of a serpent: The poison of the wicked, that's what happened to our sister Serena Williams.

They are like the deaf adder: This is what Serena didn't realize. They're like the deaf adder. The deaf adder is a snake, and being deaf, it's not hearing you. So no matter how much loving you try to give them, you Black women trying to give loving to the snake, it's not going to happen. It's not going to change him. The scriptures tell you that. Don't be in them, because they will turn your heart away from the Most High. That's what the Bible says in Deuteronomy.

That stoppeth her ear: They stop their ears up when you're trying to bring them scriptures. You're trying to make them into righteous people when they were born crooked from the womb. They were estranged, and you can't straighten them out. You cannot charm the snake.

Which will not hearken to the voice of charmers: They will not hearken, meaning they won't listen to the Bible. The charmers is the Bible. They will not hearken to the voice of charmers. Here you trying to charm the snake, and it's not listening to you. It's gonna bite you, and you know what it's going to say after it bite you? You knew I was a snake. You're looking at me like, what the hell is wrong with you? Didn't you know I was a snake? You wonder why he's dealing with you like that.

Their poison is like the poison of a serpent: Many things that we talked about, we talked about Derek Chauvin. Look at the part of the tree that says law. You see politics, genetics, history, mental testing. All of these are the roots that feed this tree. This tree is talking about the American way. It says, I'm reading the bottom of it, like a tree, eugenics draws its materials from many sources and organizes them into a harmonious entity. So don't just zero in on the, quote unquote, police department. Don't just zero in on Derek Chauvin per se, because Derek Chauvin is just one part of the root, one part of the problem. But all of them work together as a well-oiled machine in deception and evil and exploitation, robbery. They all work together to make that engine work perfectly. So don't think you can, quote unquote, reform one part of the tree and the rest of the tree is rotten. That's what Trevor Noah was saying. The so-called bad apples is not what you should be looking at. You got to look at the whole rotten tree that brings forth the apples.

Their poison is like the poison of a serpent: Part of the substance of this country derives from education. We already talked about law. History, they lied about history. Religion is in there somewhere. You got economics. All of these things work together to keep the racist system of America going. But I want to talk about education, because we talked about Chauvin: whether he would have been an ice cream man, a scientist, garbage man, whatever, he'd probably pick the garbage up from your house and throw it back on your lawn, then call you if you say something. So the mindset, it doesn't matter where they work. It's bred in them, and that's what we're going to show you now.

Their poison is like the poison of a serpent: The word eugenics means good genes. In other words, they use these different roots to kill the good genes of us and to accelerate white folks. That's all this is saying. The word gene is connected in it because it's talking about bringing forth more serpents, like we were just reading out of Psalms. And it's to kill off anything about righteousness, to kill off Israel, to kill off the truth. They put on the facade like they are about the truth: oh, we believe in the Bible, we believe in justice. But don't be fooled, brothers and sisters. This whole system is wicked as hell, and you better learn that sooner than later.

Their poison is like the poison of a serpent: Derek Chauvin, he's not by himself. All of this society think the same way. We're gonna go into the roots on how things gotten to where they've gotten. This was a book that was written by this brother named Jawanza Kunjufu, and the name of this book is called Countering the Conspiracy to Destroy Black Boys. And he makes the point in this book that the focus is centered on Black boys, because it's easy to kill the race when you're dealing with them as a boy, as opposed to waiting until he becomes a man. George Floyd is out of the way now, but it's to kill them all. If you got to lie, you got to do all kinds of things. But if you can systematically kill him as a boy, it's more subtle, and most people won't even notice it. To kill them as a male is high profile, so it's easier to destroy them when they're boys. And that's what this man brings out in this book here. The countering, it comes out of the Bible, by the way.

Their poison is like the poison of a serpent: I want to bring your attention to one of the great areas of where this destruction actually happens. When your sons go to school, you Black women, you Black men, as soon as they enter into the school system, they're full of exuberance. They're full of ingenuity. Walking geniuses. Many of our sons, many of our daughters, brilliant brainiacs. And soon as they get into what is categorized as the fourth grade syndrome, something happens, and the seeds of doubt begins to seep in. The seeds of apathy sets in. All kind of things sets in. So the question is, what happened? It's easier to kill off many George Floyds, many prophets, many engineers, many doctors. You can kill off a lot of them if you can destroy them as boys rather than waiting till they become grown. So that's the reason why the attention was focused on Black boys in particular, Black and Hispanics. The fourth grade failure syndrome: they actually coined that. Identified where the problem began.

Their poison is like the poison of a serpent: He recognized it. In other words, he was seeing it in the neighborhood, but he had to find out what is the genesis of this, so he began to pinpoint where this destruction was happening. Often so subtle. Think about our men. The majority of our people don't graduate. They end up going into the streets, into a life of crime, get locked up, and then become slaves for the state. That is by design.

Their poison is like the poison of a serpent: So they try to say that our kids don't like to learn, our kids are not on a scholastic level, we don't like analytics, we don't like numbers and math. They feed us that garbage to make us believe that we are adverse to learning, they can't learn, ADHD and all those stigmas, to destroy the aspirations of your young bright genius children.

Their poison is like the poison of a serpent: Listening to stories: there's you talking about analytics there. Once his classmate Richard was sad about an incident at home, and Daryl was quick to provide instant cheer. So they try to say that we have this, don't look at me, don't touch me. We learned that BS. But look at this here: we see our brother. He's noticing that his own brother looks like he's got some kind of problem, so he goes to the brother and he tries to consult, tries to work with him to build him up. He asked so many questions. He's enthusiastic. He loves learning. He's inquisitive about everything. That's the way our sons are. You mothers, y'all know what I'm talking about. He loves numbers and alphabet. We know how we love to read. We love mathematics.

Their poison is like the poison of a serpent: Kindergarten through third grade: this is known as the killing field. What happened here? He's losing his enthusiasm. There's something happening in the classroom, and it's something that is called teacher expectation. Remember the thing with Malcolm, when the teacher asked Malcolm what did you want to be when you grew up, and he said he wanted to be a lawyer. What did that white teacher say to him? That's a perfect example of what happened to Daryl. Just killed his aspirations right there. And that's what happens to your sons, mainly our sons, because if you kill the son, you kill the man, and you kill the nation. Our enemies understood that. They'll let the sisters grow up and then hope to do to them what they did to Serena Williams, because once they take her mind, she's gone. So they say, once the man is out of the way, the woman is spoiled.

Their poison is like the poison of a serpent: The alphabet and numbers still interest him, but now the dump truck, his bicycle and his football are now his most important possessions. Why? Because we are inculcated to worship our dump trucks and to worship basketball and things of that nature, and be more or less inclined to deal with analytics, numbers and things of that nature. That's by design. This is what happens to our children. This is why they referred to Rodney King as a lizard, as gorilla in the midst. This is the reason why Derek Chauvin dealt with that brother like that, because this is how he saw him. So this ain't got nothing to do with the police department. This is education that we're looking at. This was in books. Our teachers taught us this. They taught us about a white Christ, and then at the same time they spraying water hoses on us when we were little.

Their poison is like the poison of a serpent: They compared us to an ape. This is a Derek Chauvin in the science department of America, like it's some real science. Science say Negroes still in ape stage. Race is positively not equal. This is why Serena Williams said, I need to be equal, let me get rid of this brown so I can be equal to you. This is the damage that has happened throughout the educational system. So don't just look at the, quote unquote, police department and talk about the bad apples there. The whole damn tree is rotten. That's the point, to produce this kind of thinking, and we walk around with this kind of mess in our heads. Look at that: white Christian civilization. What the hell are they talking about? Short legs, like we don't have long legs. These are cruel images that our children will see, and they will begin to doubt their own greatness. That's the point of it.

Their poison is like the poison of a serpent: I know this hurts. I understand it. But this is what we were taught. This is what our fathers were taught. We were made to think on these kinds of levels, to the point where we can't even believe that we can work together. We feel like we can't even work together among ourselves, because we think that we are inferior, because of this kind of evil teaching that we've learned in this system. This whole rotten system, all aspects of this system, taught us to think like this.

Their poison is like the poison of a serpent: We're talking about the various knees. So you got a knee of law enforcement, a knee of education, a knee of religion. All of these knees are on us, and let me show you what these knees lead to. Dr. Joy DeGruy, this is her book, Post Traumatic Slave Syndrome. So this is basically trauma that has come after the slavery. After we have been, quote unquote, emancipated, there is a post, or an after, trauma that still rests on us. It's a traumatic syndrome that we live in. We carry a traumatic slave syndrome with us to this day, where I'm gonna bleach my skin that God gave me. That's some serious mental damage there.

Their poison is like the poison of a serpent: We're going to talk about something that's called vacant esteem. Society contributes to the formation of vacant esteem. We know vacant means absent, and esteem is a feeling within yourself of value. When you esteem yourself, you're giving value to yourselves. Well, if you're saying that your value is empty, that is, your esteem is vacant. So this is an actual psychiatry definition here.

Their poison is like the poison of a serpent: She didn't say the police department. She says society contributes to the formation, or the creation, or the whole eugenics tree. Like Trevor Noah was saying, the whole tree is rotten. Society, all of its institutions, contribute to the formation of vacant esteem in a number of ways, not just the police. Through its laws: that's one of the tree of eugenics, the legal system. Institutions, schools and policies, government. Underneath institutions you got banking institutions, economics, schools or universities. All of these things contribute to our vacant esteem. Television, cosmetics, the magazines, all of these things. As well as through the media. In other words, we make up a very small portion of the population in this country, but yet we are vastly overrepresented in the penal criminal system. There's millions of us, unproportionately to our number in this country, that fill the prisons. All that's by design. That's what I was reading about in terms of the educational system and all the different mediums by which we learn and see ourselves, religion, all of it. It contributes to our being overrepresented in the penal institutions, prisons.

Their poison is like the poison of a serpent: The media, that's part of the eugenics tree again. All of this contributes. These are the knees that's on us. Why am I going through all of this? Because our brothers and sisters need to repent. The Lord is not going to allow us to be exuberant and enjoy, oh, we got a breath of fresh air. The Lord is not bringing that to us. Don't be fooled. Displaying African Americans as criminals: don't they do that? They make us look like criminals. Cops, that's what it's about. Disadvantaged: meaning saying that we're on welfare and all this. Academically deficient: that ain't what we was reading earlier with the brother. He loved numbers, but once they kill the aspirations, then they say, oh, look at you now. After they've done the damage, then they say, look at you, and we will look at ourselves and actually internalize that and think that there's really something wrong with us academically. Sexually irresponsible: you're just laying down having babies. Where's your fathers? They're in jail. That's how they talk about us. The media puts us out there like that. We got a lot of work to do, brothers and sisters.

Their poison is like the poison of a serpent: There's another statistic out here, along with this death of our kids, and that's happening in the schools, because we talked about the conspiracy to destroy Black boys. It's happening in the school systems. If they escape it, then they kill them some other kind of way. But in addition to those terrible factors, 19 million of our babies, Black babies, have been aborted since 1973. So we got a hell of a problem going on. So ain't no such thing as me rejoicing because of one verdict. If this man get a million years, that ain't change nothing. That's just one, and like I said, they'll hang his behind just to dupe the rest of us.

Their poison is like the poison of a serpent: Sexually irresponsible: you just lay down with anybody. You ain't looking to be married. You women, you men, you just pop each other. That's what they're saying. That's how they speak about us. And sadly, we actually live this out, because we actually think that's part of some culture. So the point of the media doing this is for us to perceive ourselves in this manner. All of these and more serve to influence how we perceive ourselves, so to impact our assessment of our own worth. That's the devalue.

Their poison is like the poison of a serpent: Consider this real life example. In the summer of 1992, two teenage boys, call them Carl and Dominic, got into an argument outside of a local high school in Portland. This is about vacant esteem. She's getting ready to give you a real live event. Of course she had to change the names, but these people really did exist. Some of the behaviors is suicidal, homicidal maniac. These are some of the things that we see. Typically about nothing important: stepped on my shoes, you got a bigger piece of chicken than me. Brothers died over that damn thing. You jumped me in the line. Until Carl pulled out a gun and pointed it at Dominic's face: how in the world did Carl get a gun? Where'd Carl get a gun from? That's like Harlem, crack vials all over the place. Where the hell they get these things from? They don't make those vials in Harlem. Where did that stuff come from?

Their poison is like the poison of a serpent: He remained perfectly still as he watched Carl pull the trigger. This is what vacant esteem does. When you have no value of yourselves, you don't see your life as worthy of living. This is where drugs come in. This is where all of these things come in, where we don't care about our lives. The bad eating habits, all of these things come out of stuff like this, when you have a very low esteem about yourselves. We don't even take care of ourselves. These traumatizing knees brought us all the way down into attitudes like this. The gun jammed. Dominic didn't run. That's your time to get the hell out of there. Dominic didn't bum rush him. That's what was supposed to happen. Instead he said angrily, do you think I'm afraid to die? Listen to that suicidal answer. Why is he saying that? Because my life is worth nothing. In other words, he wanted to die. That's what that vacant esteem leads to. This is where a lot of our people are right now. Why am I bringing all of this? Because we are trying to save our people through the scriptures. We're trying to save our people, tell them, come out of her, my people, and repent, because this is not normal. The way we're living is not normal, brothers and sisters. None of this ugliness, all this abortion, all this madness that's going on, none of this is normal.

Their poison is like the poison of a serpent: Somebody's saying run, fool, but he's busy saying how bold I am. This is because his life has lined up so badly. He has no value for his life, and it's all, like I said, suicide. I'm tired of living like this here. I'd rather die. Can you believe this was true? This actually happened. This is not a story. This is not a fairy tale. I've seen stuff like this happen. Miraculously he survived. So now he gets to come back out and say, I got street cred. I can use that to build up my esteem. I didn't run. I ain't no punk. This is what all this evil has boiled us down to.

Their poison is like the poison of a serpent: When our brothers lose their esteem and lose their value, we become indifferent to each other. Remember we talked about the young boy Daryl. He saw his brother, and he saw that there was something troubling him at home, and he went to console him, try to lift his spirits up. We don't have that anymore, because that was killed through the educational system, through the compounding of the various branches of this rotten tree, that caused us to be monsters towards each other, to the point where stuff like this will happen. All of that for a doggone truck. To carjack her truck. If that woman would have put up any more resistance, they would have killed her for a truck. This is because of vacant esteem, when we think that a truck is worth somebody's life. That's how bad things have gotten.

Their poison is like the poison of a serpent: Robberies like this happen every day in Houston. So that means there's a big problem with our brothers down there. We got some work to do. This is where we got to be that beacon of light to make the change. It is incumbent upon us as men to do the things that our people need in terms of getting themselves right, because this Bible is their book. They have to learn this. This is not something that we're asking people to join per se. This is your book. This is the calibration of your whole lives. This is what's going to set your mind right, set your spirit right. But we have to do this. Our enemies ain't gonna help us do this. We got to undo stuff like this here. We got to curb abortions. Our young girls getting abducted, and you don't know what's happening to them. They're putting them in sex rings. Just because it faded from the news don't mean that it stopped. Our daughters are still being kidnapped and taken away. We still have a lot of work to do, brothers and sisters.

Their poison is like the poison of a serpent: They say that we are capricious, we just respond without thinking. They say that about us too, and that's what that example would be. But how did we get to this? We broke the laws of the Most High, and it caused these curses to come upon us, and that's the reason why it led all the way down to these kinds of situations that we see here. It's a terrible thing, but if we as men don't elect to fix these issues with our people, who's going to do it? If we ourselves don't decide right now to make the difference, when is it going to get done? It's a slur on our own manhood if we say, hey white man, come fix our problems, and we're men. We stand up here with a badge of manhood on us. That makes no sense at all.

Their poison is like the poison of a serpent: Brothers and sisters, we gotta repent. We gotta return to the Most High. The message is for our brothers and sisters to repent, return unto the Lord. The Lord said for us to gather ourselves together. That's what the scripture said in Zephaniah 2:1.

precepts.why:
This is what we have to understand.

“The earth is given into the hand of the wicked”: The Most High said that the earth is given into the hand of the wicked, so the earth is being controlled by a wicked people.

“He covereth the faces of the judges thereof”: Got rid of all of the judges, the Native American Indians, all the judges, the Israelites. He covered them all up. That's what this wicked man did. When you read the book of Malachi, it tells you that this wicked man is Edom. It's Esau. That's who he's talking about. So he's the wicked that the Bible is talking about. He is the beginning of all wickedness, so you can't change him.

“Who is he?”: Who is the wicked? If the Most High is wrong, who is the wicked?

“Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished”: Is the so-called white man. Their scholars, their biblical scholars, they know this already.

“But we will return and build the desolate places”: Out of the Renaissance, that came back and set up America on stolen property, and murdered, and covered the faces of the judges literally.

“They shall build”: They shall build up America, build up their justice system, build up their educational system, build all their systems up. Listen to what God said.

“But I will throw down”: But God said, I'm going to destroy it, in thermonuclear destruction.

“And they shall call them, The border of wickedness”: And the people all over the earth, they're going to say, woe unto him that increaseth that which is not his. That's in the book of Habakkuk. So what they shall call them? The border of wickedness. They are the people where wickedness begins. That's the reason why it says what it says in the Apocrypha, when it talked about Alexander and his four generals. It says, when they all put crowns upon themselves after Alexander died, and they ruled after them many years, and evils were multiplied in the earth. That's the precept right there. Evils were multiplied when these people started ruling.

“The border of wickedness”: They are the beginning of wickedness.

“The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever”: The whole race. God says he has indignation against the people of Edom, all of them. That's God speaking. All his descendants. That's the justice that we're looking for. So don't be happy about what's getting ready to happen to Derek Chauvin. That ain't nothing but just a play on you Negroes' emotions. But like I said, take the little bit of whatever they give us. Take it, fine. But still, that's not going to get them out of the judgment from the Most High. We just read it.
